subject: clockworkDog
pitch: A wind-up clockwork terrier made of polished brass and copper. Riveted body plates, visible gears turning in its chest, a big winding key on its back, springy jointed legs, floppy leather ears, glass-lens eyes with a green tint, a tail made of a coiled spring, and a little red collar with a brass tag.
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module using the SDK to build a terrier-like model, sketching out proportional dimensions like body length, shoulder height, and scale relative to a real terrier.

Now I'm working through the skeleton hierarchy - placing a hips root joint, then building a spine chain with catmull-spline points running toward the chest, followed by a neck chain extending up toward the head, making sure parent-child joint relationships are consistent.

For the head and jaw, I'm defining joints using local coordinates relative to the head's forward-facing orientation, aiming for a terrier-like forward jaw placement while being careful about which axis represents forward versus up.

For the legs, I'm working out a four-legged structure with front shoulders and hind hips, calculating joint positions and limb bend directions so the front elbows bend backward and the hind knees bend forward then back at the hock, mimicking natural dog leg anatomy before building the chains.

I'm working out the bend directions for each leg's inner joints, keeping front legs curling the same way and alternating hind leg bends for a digitigrade look. Then I'm planning to sweep each leg chain with tapered brass radii, and shift to building the body itself as a loft along the spine chain with station widths and heights defined at each spine point.

I'm sketching out the station positions along the body length, roughly tripling the toy-scale proportions to feel more like a real terrier, and figuring out how to bind the loft to the spine chain using the bone parameter so the body skins to the spine curve properly. I still need to reconcile the spine chain's starting point with where the body stations begin, since the hips root and the loft stations don't quite line up yet.

Now I'm working out the hierarchy: setting the hips root at the start of the spine path, parenting the hind leg sockets to that same region even though they sit at a different z, then building out the neck chain from the end of the spine to support the head joint.

For the head itself, I'm sketching a loft of stations moving forward along the bone to form a tapered skull shape, then adding a separate frustum-box snout extending further forward for that terrier-style elongated muzzle.

For the eyes, I'm placing glass-lens spheres with a green tint on the head bone, then wrapping a small brass bezel ring around each one using a ring helper to scatter tiny decorative elements around the eye's circumference.

Now I'm working out orientation for the brass torus bezel so its face points outward from the head, then moving on to design floppy leather ears with a drooping extruded outline attached near the top sides of the head.

Now I'm working out where to place the winding key on the back, calculating the body's top height so the key base sits correctly, then designing its shape as a lathed post with a loop-like ring on top, similar to a classic wind-up toy key.

For visible gears, I'm thinking through adding a star-shaped gear outline on the chest front, alternating inner and outer radii to form teeth, then extruding it into a thin plate with beveled edges to sit behind a window cutout.

Rather than a single front-facing gear colliding with the neck, I'm repositioning two gears onto the body's flanks instead, mirroring their placement and orientation across the x-axis so one sits on each side of the chest.

I'll also add a smaller meshing gear in a contrasting copper color behind the main one for visual depth, with a helper function to generate gear outline points by alternating outer and inner radius vertices.

For the body plates, I'm thinking riveted bands wrapped around the body using surface loop cuts positioned at spine joints, with the loop plane oriented perpendicular to the spine's local axis so the band wraps naturally around the form.

For the rivets themselves, I'd scatter small spheres along the loop path at regular intervals, orienting each one with stick so it seats properly on the surface with the rim embedded slightly for a riveted look.

For the plates, I'm planning several rim bands at different points along the body's length, each requiring a surface derived from the body loft mesh.

For legs, I'm considering making them springy by wrapping copper coil rings around brass tubes using a torus geometry placed along the leg chain, needing to figure out the correct orientation frame for each coil.

Good, so the frame orientation puts the local +Y axis along the tangent, confirming that rotating the torus geometry to put its axis on Y will align it correctly with the frame. For the legs, I'll sweep coils along each limb chain between specific fractional points to give a springy appearance, and for the tail I'm thinking of building a spiral path going back and up from the hips to create a coiled spring look.

Writing coil placement code...

I still need to figure out the collar: it should loop around the neck, but since there's no explicit neck mesh yet, I'll need to build the neck as its own tapered sweep first before placing the collar ring around it.

Then I'm working out where to anchor a hanging brass tag off the front of the collar, figuring out whether collar points give me a usable frame for extrusion—since chain points seem to convert to frames, I can likely use the neck chain's tangent frame directly for positioning.

Positioning the tag below and forward of the neck frame, orienting its face outward, and sketching a simple polygon disc shape for the tag body with a slight bevel, skipping any extra engraving or ring details for now.

Now I'm placing the nose as a small dark sphere right at the snout's tip, the eyes as glass-lens spheres partially sunk into the sides of the head, and settling on a brass/copper/leather color palette for the body, keeping the material solid rather than adding stripes or gradients.

I'm deciding to add a mottled patina texture to the copper and brass body parts for a weathered look, trimming down my imports to just the essentials (builder, limb, mottle, catmull), and working out the leg joint hierarchy with brass paw-cap spheres sized to match the foot tip joints.

I'm figuring out the leg segment counts and lengths: each limb returns four points forming three spans, so I need four joint names per leg including the tip. For the hind legs, I'm calculating segment lengths against the hip-to-foot vertical distance to make sure the total reach works out with proper bending.

For the front legs I'm doing similar math from shoulder to foot height, then setting bend directions for the knee and wrist joints. I'm mirroring left/right sides using a sign variable and deciding how to name each chain, and now I'm working out which spine joint should parent the front legs versus the hips parenting the hind legs, based on where the spine's catmull-rom knots land.

I'm expanding the spine into four points for three joints, then building the neck as its own catmull chain parented to the last spine joint, and placing the head joint at the neck's end with a forward-and-slightly-up direction. I'm also starting to position the jaw joint relative to the head using local forward/up offsets.

Now I'm detailing the robot dog's full geometry: jaw and snout as frustum boxes bolted to the head bone, a scaled sphere for the skull, extruded ear shapes with a drooping outline flared outward from the sides, glass eye spheres with brass torus bezels, and a small nose sphere. I'm also laying out mechanical details like meshing gear pairs extruded onto the body's side plates, a winding key made from a lathed post and torus ring on the back, a coiled spring tail built from a sweep core with torus rings threaded along it, rivet bands and loop seams around the body surface, and finally a collar made from a surface loop with a hanging tag extruded as a thin plate in front of the neck.

Now I'm writing the full build script: defining color constants for brass, copper, red, leather, glass, and dark tones, setting up the joint skeleton (hips, spine chain, neck chain, head, jaw), building the body as a loft between stations, generating front and hind leg chains procedurally for both sides using inverse-kinematics-style limb helpers, sweeping brass tubes along each leg with copper coil rings, capping feet with copper spheres bound to each leg's tip joint, and finishing with rivet bands and sphere studs looped around the body surface at several points along the spine.

Still writing build script...
